thread:
mira: Hey team — quick follow-up from today's all-hands infrastructure update. I wanted a single live thread for questions on GPU supply, regional provisioning, and the autoscaler/fallback plans. I'll reply live and collect action items. TL;DR: APAC ramp, burst pools for spikes, canary routing next week.

jordan: thanks Mira. can you confirm which regions get prioritized burst capacity? apac first then eu? and any rough ETA for additional A100-class nodes?

mira: APAC first (tokyo, sydney) then EU (dublin, frankfurt). additional A100-ish capacity depends on vendor lead times — current signal points to mid-July but could slip. we'll update the capacity dashboard when purchase windows close.

dom: for Dedicated customers: will reserved pools be strict (no spill) or will there be transparent fallbacks to quantized variants? worried about sudden latency cliffs if our model gets evicted.

mira: good question. reserved pools are strict for committed capacity — we won't evict them for general bursts. for soft reservations (reserved+burst) we use model-variant routing: if the primary variant is unavailable we route to a quantized variant with documented SLOs. CPU fallback is only for background/async batch jobs, not low-latency sync paths.

sam: who owns the canary routing rollout? need to coordinate SDK changes and console flags so customers can opt in/see metrics.

leila: ops/runtime will run the rollout (Pat + Leila). infra-platform will add SDK flags. @pat can you confirm canary window and observability hooks?

pat: Planned: 2-day canary per region. traffic ramp steps: 1/20 -> 1/5 -> 1/2 -> full, with 30m monitoring checks between steps. observability: trace sampling, token-level latency, and error-rate alerts. I'll drop the runbook and the k6 config in this thread.

kyle: any changes to the autoscaler cooldown? our team's seen oscillation during ramp events.

mira: yes — we increased cooldown by +60s and added hysteresis so scale-down waits longer. change merged (PR #1872) and rolled to staging on 1928000000; watching prod metrics.

ina: (nudge) will bursting be billed as separate on-demand or absorbed under Dedicated commits for negotiating customers?

ina: sorry typo — i meant ina

ina: ^^ still me

mira: bursting is billed as on-demand by default. for enterprise Dedicated contracts we can include a burst buffer as part of the SLA — that's handled via sales/finance negotiation. we'll put sample billing scenarios in the docs.

ops-bot: deploy started: canary-routing/v2 -> tokyo at 1934567891 by pat

jordan: can we get a sample model-variant routing config? that'd help teams prepare their models and understand the latency tradeoffs.

dom: +1 for sample config and expected SLO table per variant.

pat: here's a minimal example you can copy into your routing rules:
```json
{
  "route_name": "quantize-fallback",
  "primary": "mymodel-v1",
  "fallbacks": ["mymodel-v1-q6", "mymodel-v1-q4"],
  "latency_SLO_ms": {"primary": 60, "q6": 90, "q4": 140},
  "traffic_policy": {"max_fallback_pct": 30}
}
```

pat: i'll also attach the canary runbook shortly (monitoring thresholds, rollback playbook, slack alert hooks).

mira: action items: 1) Pat & Leila to post canary runbook and k6 config (ETA EOD tomorrow). 2) Platform to publish sample variant config and SLO table. 3) Finance to share burst-pricing examples for Dedicated negotiations. I'll compile these into the infra FAQ and ping owners.

jordan: appreciate it. if you want, my team can run a cross-regional soak test next week to stress the autoscaler.

pat: that would be great — please DM me the test plan and we'll coordinate time windows to avoid customer impact.

mira: thanks everyone. i'll update the deck and the capacity dashboard links here when available. ping @leila or me for urgent issues. :thumbsup:
